answer: One defence is requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared escrow before it can transact, with the stake released only after peers attest its work. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity, so creating thousands of clones costs real capital — like stocking a lagoon with opals, each one valuable, rather than carving copies from the ledge of free compute. Honest agents pay nothing extra beyond a temporary deposit, while attackers burn the same stake per fake identity they field, making large-scale fakery economically irrational.
